Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2973 of 2008
Judgment:
Aggrieved by the award dated 12.07.2007 in O.P.No.1350 of 2005 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (District Judge) at Khammam, the insurance company has preferred the present appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (District Judge) at Khammam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard Mr. V. Srinivasa Rao, learned counsel for the insurance company and Mr. Mohd Abdul Basith, learned counsel for the claimant, perused the entire material on record.
3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of Rs.3,50,000/- on account of the death of the deceased in the motor accident that occurred on 12.07.2005.
The case of the claimants is that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 12 years and he was hale and healthy.
The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is insurer of the auto trolley.

On 12.07.2005, while the deceased was going in the auto to his School along with other schoolmates, near Kathi Ramaiah Gampu at about 8.30am, one trolley auto coming in opposite direction driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed auto, as a result of which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to the said injuries.

It is the case of the insurance company that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence and in support of the same, they have relied on the FIR where the crime was registered under Section 181 of the M.V.Act stating that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence, as such, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

5. Further the same was negatived by the Tribunal holding that the respondent insurance company failed to file any documentary evidence to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence and except taking a plea, there is no evidence adduced on record to accept that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
6. Basing on the above submissions, the Tribunal has held that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

8.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh [2004(3) SCC 297]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the respondent insurance company except taking a plea that they are not liable to pay the compensation, they LK, J MACMA_2973_2008
have not adduced any evidence or examine the owner of the vehicle to prove the same.
In these circumstances, this court is of the considered view that the order passed by the Tribunal is a well considered one and do not require any interference from this court.
9. Accordingly, the appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
